Violation ID: 8286558
Permit API: 021-20870
Unconventional: No
County: Cambria

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/25/2026
Comments: On 8/25/2026, the Department conducted a surface inspection of the Gergely 1 well in Munster Township, Cambria County. This inspection was conducted in response to a Notice of Intent (NOI) to plug the well received on 8/18/2026.This inspection is not evaluating compliance with Order 450586, as it is being overseen by the OG SubSurface team.At the time of inspection, the following was observed:- A rig is staged on site for plugging operations. A dark, oily fluid was observed at one of the plugging rig controls. The Department recommends that the Operator monitor this portion of the plugging rig and take necessary measures to prevent a fluid release to the ground.- The access road and well site are heavily rutted, which appears to be caused by vehicles and machinery that were tracked-in for well plugging operations. No site stabilization measures, such as gravel, have been implemented anywhere on site.- It appears that no perimeter Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) controls were installed on site prior to starting earth disturbances related to well plugging operations. No E and S/Restoration plan was observed on site during this inspection.- No evidence of a fluid leak, such as staining, was observed on the ground around the gas well. The API number was not observed on site.- The Operator's information required by OGA 3211(G) was not observed on site. The Department recommends that the Operator post their information on site in accordance with OGA 3211(G), until plugging operations are complete and the Certificate of Well Plugging (COWP) is approved by DEP Oil and Gas Inspector (OGI).Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued against the heavy tire rutting and for failure to have the E and S/Restoration plan available on site.While on site, the Department spoke via phone with Operator representative Chris Caskey and informed them of the Department's observations and forthcoming violations in this inspection report. The outstanding violations issued for failure to post the API number and operator's information on site are being overseen by the OG SubSurface team.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 966784
Permit API: 129-24375
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Derry Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/26/2022
Comments: On August 26, 2022, the Department conducted an inspection on the Janoscrat 1 well in Derry Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection CEI inspection in response to violations issued under inspection 3400883 where violations were issued due to a possible brine discharge that was discovered on July 29, 2022. The following was observed:The brine tank from where the possible discharge occurred in inspection 3400883 has since been removed, and the area has been mulched and seeded (see photos 1 and 2). The hissing sound and gas odor previously noted on the well head in inspections 3400883 and 3399998 is no longer present (see photo 4). Newly updated operator's information has also been added (see photo 3). Soil conductivity readings were taken on both sides of what once appeared to be the brine puddle. The one taken on the side closest to the well at the former location of the brine tank read, .49 Micro Siemens (see photo 6). The one taken on the side farthest away from the well read .44 Micro Siemens (see photo 7). An additional reading was taken on the side closest to the well at the former brine tank location, but approximately 6 inches of soil was dug before the reading was taken. It read .38 Micro Siemens. A background reading was taken 50 feet west of the well which read .24 Micro Siemens (see photo 9). Overall, the conductivity of the soil at the site of the possible brine release appears to now be comparable to the surrounding soil.Based on observations from today's inspection, the impacted soil appears to have been removed as of August 26, 2022. However, outstanding violations issued during inspection record 3400883 shall remain open since no NOV response or any of the information requested has been received from the operator.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/27/2023 to LEATHERWOOD LLC in Morris Township, Greene county. OGA3220(A) - PLUGGING REQUIREMENTS - Failure to plug the well upon abandoning it.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: LEATHERWOOD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/27/2023
Violation Code: OGA3220(A) - PLUGGING REQUIREMENTS - Failure to plug the well upon abandoning it.
Violation ID: 8160961
Permit API: 059-28128
Unconventional: No
County: Greene
Municipality: Morris Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/27/2023
Comments: The Department conducted an inspection of the Leatherwood LLC, Stockdale 1 gas well on 9/27/2023. The well is properly identified. The well is not equipped for production. On site a closed top frac tank is present. A 2" steel line is connected to the top of the 4 1/2" production casing. The 4 1/2" x 7" production annulus is shut in. The 2" steel line extends from the well to an access hatch on top of the frac tank. Based on the position of the wellhead valve, the 4 1/2" production casing appears to be venting into the frac tank. Fluid is visible in the bottom of the frac tank. The volume of fluid in the tank could not be determined. At the access hatch on top of the frac tank, 2% LEL methane and 10 ppm carbon monoxide was detected. 23% methane and 166 ppm carbon monoxide was detected at the open end of the 2" steel line at the the frac tank hatch opening. At the well, no methane gas was detected. No leaks or odors were observed or noted at or around the well. The Stockdale 1 gas well is abandoned. The well has not been used to produce, extract or inject any gas, petroleum or other liquid within the preceding 12 months and has never been equipped for production upon completion. A Notice of Violation is being issued to the operator for failure to plug the well upon abandoning it.

The ERP and PPC plan appear to contain the sections required by 78a.55. Seven gas wells are on site that appear to be equipped for production (photo 12). Well 6H is equipped with a well tag with no observable evidence of a fluid leak to the ground around it (photos 24 and 25). The well and operator's information are displayed and visible on this well tag, as required by OGA 3211(g) and OGA 3211(h).The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (photo 12). The GPU/Vertical Separator Units on site are equipped with interconnected secondary containment drip pans (photos 13 and 14). This form of GPU secondary containment was approved by the Department for use on 6/21/2022.Based on observations from this inspection, violations are being issued against the slough on the cutslope above the access road.The following information is requested from the operator:- What is being done in the interim (temporary stabilization)- What is being done in the future (permanent stabilization)Please coordinate with DEP Technical Services for any potential modifications to the approved ESP that may be necessary for addressing the slough.

Comments: On April 19, 2024, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a spill report that was received by the Department on April 18, 2024 at 7:50 PM. The report states the spill, that reportedly occurred on April 18, 2024 at approximately 6:10 PM, was approximately 15 gallons of hydraulic fluid. Act 9 sign is present on site (Photo 1). PPC and ERP plans are both present on site (Photos 2-3).The Department was met on site by Derek Zofchak and Nick Reda of Range Resources, along with other crew who were working on the hydraulic line repair of the bulldozer on site. According to the operator, approximately 15 gallons of hydraulic fluid was released to the ground from a bulldozer during construction activities. The bulldozer unexpectedly stopped as it was tracking over a newly graded area of the site when the crew observed the hydraulic fluid on the ground where the dozer had been traveling. Range Resources then scraped approximately 2-3 inches of the newly graded and now impacted soil and placed it into two roll off boxes, which have been since removed from the site to be disposed. The area of impact can be seen in Photos 4-7 where the soil is no longer tracked on top. According to Range Resources, the bulldozer remains at the location where it shut down, as pictured, while a crew is actively working to repair the line. Violations are being noted and immediately corrected. The Department requests disposal documents when they are made available to the Operator.

Inspection Date: 7/27/2021
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator of a release of an estimated 5 gallons of hydraulic fluid to the pad surface on Pad B. This inspection was only conducted on Pad B. I met with EQT Company Man Bill Mitchell upon arriving on location. He showed me the location of the release which was along the edge of the well site secondary containment in the travel lane near the company man trailer. The area had already been scraped and backfilled at the time of this inspection. The company man said that the release had occurred from a radiator on a cement truck that was offloading into the upright cement tanks at the time. The truck was straddling the edge of the well site secondary containment so the fluid leaked onto the pad surface. The cement trucks were moved onto the secondary containment as of this inspection. Violations noted and considered immediately corrected. The sump that is in place on the opposite side of the pad surface has had a metal lid placed on it. This sump was installed after fluid with elevated conductivity was discovered by the Department in that area of the pad. The electrical conductivity of the fluid in the sump was approximately 1350 uS/cm. The area around the sump on the pad surface was dry during this inspection. Violations remain outstanding in association with this release.

properties.content:

Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/02/2026
Comments: On 6/2/2026, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alteration inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 60 degrees and clear when I arrived on location. When I arrived at the active north pad, I met with Seneca's Mark McCormick who described current operations as follows: Evolution Well Services has been on site since 2/13/2026, performing stimulation operations on eight recently drilled gas wells. The crew was currently alternating between the 70HU, 204HU, 203HU, and had just finished the 72HU on 6/1/2026. The crew has completed the stages on the other four wells. Mark expects stimulation activities on the eight wells to be completed by 6/9/2026.Stimulation operations were being conducted within secondary containment. There were 32 frac tanks stationed in secondary containment on the west side of the pad, four for freshwater and 28 for produced water. Additionally, there were four pump down frac tanks, two gas buster frac tanks and five working frac tanks staged in secondary containment on the pad. Chemical tanks and totes were staged in secondary containment.Five wells have been completed at the site and were staged for production. Two produced water tanks and five GPUs that are connected to the completed wells were stationed in secondary containment.Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Sediment trap 3 and the sediment basin did have standing water. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. The original south pad and access road for the Taft 851 1V well have been returned to original grade, the well pad and associated diversion berms were adequately stabilized. Separate construction projects are underway, installing water and gas pipelines on the south side of the pad.During the inspection, I field screened the following for conductivity: A 2' x 3' puddle of water above the center outfall from the north side of the pad, tested at 7.81 mS conductance. Liquid flowing from the center north outfall into the basin tested at 8.08 mS conductance. Liquid in the basin near the northeast outfall tested at 4.04 mS conductance. I met Seneca's Jeff Passerrello on location during the inspection. He was collecting water samples from the location. I discussed my findings with him.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations. The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth. I left the site at 1200 hours.

Inspection Date: 3/06/2024
Comments: On March 6, 2024, inspection conducted in response to a complaint (CTS-374226) on the Terence Shaffer 1-P041 well in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County. The following was observed:The well site was flooded by rainwater at the time of inspection (see photos 4 and 13). This did not appear to result in sedimentation on the well site during the time of inspection. The well site exhibited less than 70 percent vegetative growth coverage at the time of inspection. A gas odor was detected onsite. Hissing and bubbling was observed coming from the well head (see photos 2 and 3). The well API number and operator's information was posted on the meter box (see photo 6). However, the onsite posting lacked the operator's address. Little to no vegetative growth coverage was observed on the earthen berm surrounding the brine tank (see photos 7 and 8). A cotton-like substance was observed stuffed into one of the brine tank valves, with water flowing out of this valve (see photo 9). No elevated conductivity readings were detected underneath either brine tank valve, or anywhere onsite (see photos 5, 11, 12, and 14). Tire rutting that was severely eroded to bare stone was observed in the access road entrance (see photo 15). Sediment-laden pooling was observed in these ruts at a low point in the access road (see photo 16). An apparent stream or tributary flows through a culvert underneath this point in the access road. This sediment-laden pooling could be observed flowing from the access road ruts into this apparent stream/tributary at the culvert outlet, resulting in a discharge to the Waters of the Commonwealth (see photos 17 and 18). Department vehicles were not used to access the well site or access road for this inspection.The Department recommends that the operator post their address onsite, as is required by current regulations. OGI follow-up is being requested for evaluation of well integrity.Violations are being issued against the brine tank onsite, as it appears that it would fail to keep production fluids contained. Additional violations are being issued for failing to permanently stabilize the well site and access road, resulting in a sediment-laden discharge to the Waters of the Commonwealth.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Chief Oil & Gas Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2018-12-03
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 835137
Permit API: 015-23371
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Wilmot Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2018-12-04
Comments: Arrived onsite at 10:43 in response to a spill notification received on 12/3/18 at 15:45. Peg Farrell reported a release of about 25 gallons of brine water off of containment at the northeast corner of the pad near the produced water tanks and sand vac. The impacted area included a portion of the a collection ditch at the edge of the pad. Chief was in the process of stimulating the 4H well. Met with Colter, Company Man onsite and Kellon, Environmental Field Coordinator. They believed the cause of the spill to be from an overflowed blender. The overflow then leaked through containment and onto the pad surface. There are two layers of containment under the equipment (plastic, felt, plastic, felt). Chief will continue to inspect the containment during operations and repair any punctures or tears found. The vac truck onsite removed pooled water from the containment as soon as the spill was noticed. At the time of inspection an excavator was removing the impacted area of the pad. The area being excavated was approximately 8 ft. wide, 15 ft. long, and 2 in. deep (Photo #1). At the time of inspection about 10 to 15 cubic feet of soil had been removed. It was expected that 20 to 25 cubic feet would be removed in total. A Hanna Instruments Soil Conductivity Tester (S/N: L02110754) was used to screen the nearby area and it appeared that contamination was limited to the area immediately around the excavation (Photos #2, 3). The 5H well is scheduled to be stimulated following the 4H. Operations are expected to be completed Sunday afternoon (12/9/18). Chief is planning to pull additional containment under the blender and around the contaminated area the following Monday or Tuesday (12/10 or 12/11) to conduct additional screening of the pad surface. Violations noted and immediately corrected.

Comments: On February 29, 2024, DEP representative Brad Kline, Erica Lutz, and Evan Buck conducted a routine site inspection at the STL Resources Sturgis South Pad. The inspection is also to follow up with a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of the well pad on January 8, 2022. The conductivity of the accumulated water in the northwest stormwater vault was 851 uS/cm. The conductivity of the accumulated water in the southwest stormwater vault was 651 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 (3) had conductivity of 20.9 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 (2) had a conductivity of 21.6 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 (1) had a conductivity of 15.4 uS/cm. Stream 1 control site had a conductivity of 20 uS/cm. Seep 1 had a conductivity of 95.2 uS/cm. Seep 1a had a conductivity of 78.7 uS/cm. Seep 2 had a conductivity of 36.5 uS/cm. Seep 3 had a conductivity of 29.6 uS/cm. Seep 4 had a conductivity of 48.2 uS/cm. Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/04/2025
Comments: On November 4, 2025, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident inspection at the EQT ARO LLC Harry Stryker Well Pad. This inspection is a follow up to a 5 gallon produced fluid spill that was reported by EQT on November 3, 2025. According to EQT, the spill occurred on November 2, 2025 when a spring on the pressure relief hose failed on a tanker truck and caused produced fluid to spill on two separate areas of the access road to the Harry Stryker Well Pad. At the time of the inspection, the two areas had already been excavated and back filled with clean stone. The DEP screened the two areas where the produced fluid leaked with a soil conductivity meter. The areas did not result in a conductivity over 200 uS/cm. Area 1 appeared to be excavated approximately 30 ft. by 6 ft. Area 2 appeared to be excavated approximately 15 ft. by 4 ft. It appeared that EQT contractors only had to scrape the surface of the impacted areas to remove the impacted soil. The contaminated soil had been hauled offsite for disposal. Violations of Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and Solid Waste Management Act 301 noted but were immediately corrected.

Report Details

Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 903929
Permit API: 003-22234
Unconventional: Yes
County: Allegheny
Municipality: Forward Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/06/2021
Comments: This inspection is taking place in response to a spill reported by the operator on 12/27/2020 as well as a follow up to a previously reported spill from 8/15/2020 which has been reported as remediated. The operator reported that the spill occurred at approximately 9:30 PM when a check valve washed out. The operator reported approximately 1 barrel of Production Fluid was discharged to the ground. When asked via phone on 12/28/2020, Mr. Hardy reported that the operator would remediate the spill in accordance with Act 2. The following is observed: The Act 9 Sign is present, the ERP, PPC, and associated SDS are in the mailbox adjacent (Photo 1). The operator has removed material between GPUs 2H and 3H (Photo 2) thereby constructing a sump approximately a foot and a half deep and nearly the length of the GPU (Photo 11). Background readings taken in the area were between 70 uS and 300 uS (Photo 12 & 13). Readings taken in the vicinity of standing water in the sump were between 2,000 uS and 13,500 uS. Readings of 2,000 uS were detected between the skids of GPU 3H (Photo 16 & 17). GPU 3H is attached to GPU 16H, on the other side of this structure between another piece of Production Equipment was another smaller "sump" (Photo 6). Background in this area was around 500 uS (Photo 7). Readings taken around this sump were detected at 7,000 uS to 13,000 uS (Photo 5 & 8). GPUs 3H and 16H do not appear to have adequate secondary containment. Per the CO&A entered into on 12/17/2020, these are noted as ICS. The Department requests information on how the operator is going to remediate the impacted material in accordance with 91.33(B) and submit it before 1/11/21. Additionally, the Department requests more information on how the discharge reached the other side of 16H and how the operator intends to remediate any impacted material below the GPUs. The Department requests information on how the amount spilled was quantified. The Department also requests a copy of the waste manifest once it is available. In reference to the 8/15/2020 spill, it appears that sump has been back filled (Photo 19). The Department requests documentation including photographs of the remediation effort prior to filling in the excavated area and including conductivity readings adjacent to and under the GPU. Based on this inspection, violations are being issued for the discharge to the ground associated with GPU 3H. Violations associated with the spill that occurred on 8/15/2020 and referenced in IR 3096843 will remain outstanding. Pending the operators response, further violations may be issued.

Permit API: 015-23526
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Wilmot Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 10/13/2020
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that approximately 60-70 gallons of diesel spilled to the pad surface. A frac is on-going on this location. Upon arriving on location, I met with company man Josh Lumbardo. He showed me the location of the release which was tarped due to the rain. Mark Patty, HSE for Chesapeake, then arrived. Mr. Patty said that he believed it was an estimated 65 gallons of diesel released from a diesel delivery truck. An estimated 40 gallons of that is believed to have impacted the surface while the remainder was contained on a piece of secondary containment. A portion of pad material was excavated, placed on secondary containment on the pad, and tarped. Mr. Patty said that Creston Environmental was contracted to investigate the release and to take samples from the pad surface. He also stated that diesel was observed leaching out from beneath the rig mats adjacent to the area of the release. Mr. Patty said that the rig mats would likely be removed as soon as the frac was completed, which he estimates will take 10 more days. Then the area beneath the rig mats will be investigated to assess the extent of the impact. Beneath the tarp on the impacted area of the pad, the fluid appeared to have a gray sheen, it felt oily, and had a faint diesel odor. During this inspection, I recommended to Mr. Patty that they install a sump in the impacted area of the pad and remove fluid from the sump and the surrounding area on an as-needed basis.The Department recommends removing as many rig mats as possible adjacent to the impacted pad area as soon as possible, prior to the completion of the frac, to assess the extent of the impact and to remove any material impacted by the release.The Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation in accordance 78a.66 due to the unknown extent of the impact to the pad surface which undermines the ability to accurately estimate the spill volume.Violations noted.

Upon arriving on location, I met with company man Josh Lumbardo. He showed me the location of the release which was tarped due to the rain. Mark Patty, HSE for Chesapeake, then arrived. Mr. Patty said that he believed it was an estimated 65 gallons of diesel released from a diesel delivery truck. An estimated 40 gallons of that is believed to have impacted the surface while the remainder was contained on a piece of secondary containment. A portion of pad material was excavated, placed on secondary containment on the pad, and tarped. Mr. Patty said that Creston Environmental was contracted to investigate the release and to take samples from the pad surface. He also stated that diesel was observed leaching out from beneath the rig mats adjacent to the area of the release. Mr. Patty said that the rig mats would likely be removed as soon as the frac was completed, which he estimates will take 10 more days. Then the area beneath the rig mats will be investigated to assess the extent of the impact. Beneath the tarp on the impacted area of the pad, the fluid appeared to have a gray sheen, it felt oily, and had a faint diesel odor. During this inspection, I recommended to Mr. Patty that they install a sump in the impacted area of the pad and remove fluid from the sump and the surrounding area on an as-needed basis.The Department recommends removing as many rig mats as possible adjacent to the impacted pad area as soon as possible, prior to the completion of the frac, to assess the extent of the impact and to remove any material impacted by the release.The Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation in accordance 78a.66 due to the unknown extent of the impact to the pad surface which undermines the ability to accurately estimate the spill volume.Violations noted.

Inspection Date: 2020-02-24
Comments: Chief Oil & Gas reported a release of approximately 2 barrels of produced fluid at the Czop Pad on 2/21/20. The release occurred the same day it was reported. I arrived onsite at 10:05 on 2/24/20. I talked with Kellon Balum and Darrin, both of Chief when I arrived. The release occurred when a piece of the B section of the well broke and allowed produced fluid to begin to spray onto the pad (Photo #1, center). This section of the wellhead is not typically used and doesn't receive much gas flow. It usually is used for monitoring certain pressures in the well. It is believed that sand flowing up from the well eroded and weakened a portion of the pipe and allowed it to rupture. Gas, at approximately 700 to 800 psi pushed produced fluid through the opening, about 2 inches in diameter. This mist was somewhat directional but was blown over a large portion of the pad by wind. The release occurred sometime between a crew leaving the site and the site operator, Darrin, arriving. This limits the duration of the release to no more than about 1 hour. Based on the time and rate of release Chief believes approximately 2 barrels of fluid were released. Typically, offsite monitoring equipment is used to detect events such as this, however, equipment was frozen, and the event was undetected. Much of the pad was covered by snow and ice and beginning Friday night (2/21/20) Chief was removing the impacted snow, and excavating the pad as needed (Photo #2). They are continuing to screen with a soil conductivity meter and are removing any impacted soil. The soil is currently on containment and will be covered until containers are brought to the pad and the material is disposed of in a landfill (Photo #3. 4). Due to the volume of the release, Chief is required to pursue site remediation in accordance with 25 Pa. Code § 78a.66(c). The result of this inspection is Violations noted.

Violation ID: 877792
Permit API: 113-20278
Unconventional: Yes
County: Sullivan
Municipality: Fox Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2020-02-24
Comments: Chief Oil & Gas reported a release of approximately 2 barrels of produced fluid at the Czop Pad on 2/21/20. The release occurred the same day it was reported. I arrived onsite at 10:05 on 2/24/20. I talked with Kellon Balum and Darrin, both of Chief when I arrived. The release occurred when a piece of the B section of the well broke and allowed produced fluid to begin to spray onto the pad (Photo #1, center). This section of the wellhead is not typically used and doesn't receive much gas flow. It usually is used for monitoring certain pressures in the well. It is believed that sand flowing up from the well eroded and weakened a portion of the pipe and allowed it to rupture. Gas, at approximately 700 to 800 psi pushed produced fluid through the opening, about 2 inches in diameter. This mist was somewhat directional but was blown over a large portion of the pad by wind. The release occurred sometime between a crew leaving the site and the site operator, Darrin, arriving. This limits the duration of the release to no more than about 1 hour. Based on the time and rate of release Chief believes approximately 2 barrels of fluid were released. Typically, offsite monitoring equipment is used to detect events such as this, however, equipment was frozen, and the event was undetected. Much of the pad was covered by snow and ice and beginning Friday night (2/21/20) Chief was removing the impacted snow, and excavating the pad as needed (Photo #2). They are continuing to screen with a soil conductivity meter and are removing any impacted soil. The soil is currently on containment and will be covered until containers are brought to the pad and the material is disposed of in a landfill (Photo #3. 4). Due to the volume of the release, Chief is required to pursue site remediation in accordance with 25 Pa. Code § 78a.66(c). The result of this inspection is Violations noted.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Repsol's Broadleaf Holdings (01-115) well site located in Troy, Springfield and Columbia Townships, Bradford County on 7/1/2025 at 1010 hours. The weather was 82 degrees F with partly cloudy skies. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported by the operator. Complaints Tracking System (CTS) ID #390186 is tied to this reported release within CTS.Repsol reported to the DEP reporting hotline that on 6/30/2025 at ~0515 hours a failed gasket on a poly line caused a release of ~20 gallons of produced water to the pad surface, outside of secondary containment. An area estimated at 8 feet by 10 feet was impacted. According to Repsol, Resource Environmental was onsite 6/30/2025 to screen the area and oversee excavation efforts. Additional screening and excavation was scheduled to be completed later in the day on 7/1/2025. The poly line with the gasket that failed can be seen in photo #1. During my inspection, a representative with Repsol showed me the impacted area. I field measured some pooled fluid within the impacted area for electrical conductivity which returned a reading of ~12.67mS/cm. I also field measured pad material within the impacted area which returned readings ranging from 0.8 to 2.4mS/cm. Photo #2 shows the area that was impacted before remediation was completed. A Repsol representative later provided me photos of the area after remediation was complete via email. Resource Environmental confirmed through onsite screening that the release was cleaned up to visible. Photos #3 and 4 (provided by Repsol) show the area after remediation was completed.Based on the reported release of ~20 gallons of produced water to the pad surface and Repsol's timely remedial response, violations of the following are cited as immediately corrected against API #015-23890:Clean Streams Law 402(b)Solid Waste Management Act 30125 Pa. Code 78a.57(a)I departed the site at 1045 hours.

Comments: This well was drilled in an agricultural area off of Cider Mill Road in November/December 2007.On 10/24/22, an NOV was issued to Stonehaven Energy when it was discovered that the brine tank had been allowed to overflow. Three roll-off containers remain on-site, and it appears that remediation has been completed. No soil sample documentation has been received by the Department as of this date, and heavy deer tracks at the restored site indicate that there may still be some residual contamination. All documentation regarding the Act 2 clean-up of this site should be submitted to the Department as soon as it is available.The well has been tagged with the correct DEP permit number. The original violations regarding the spill at the site have been superseded by the administrative order.Since the most recent inspection of this site on 12/6/2023 (Inspection Record # 3655836), there have been no changes at the site. New violations have been issued during this inspection for failure to comply with an issued court order, failure to plug the well upon abandonment, and for failure to submit annual production information.

Permit API: 085-23523
Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/24/2021
Comments: Stopped to inspect this gas well a day after the reported spill incident as the result of a piece of farm equipment had that had hit this gas well causing a release of gas and production fluids. The incident happened at approximately 11 AM on June 23, 2021. I was notified the same day by phone at 1 PM by Matt Kleese from Diamond Energy. The summary of the situation is as follows: the gas well was hit by a piece of equipment being operated by Centerra Co-op for the farmer. The tubing on the gas well was completely sheared off by this piece of equipment. Nobody was injured. The gas well had an approximate pressure of 680 psi and vented for approximately 1 minute after the incident before it just basically stopped. Centerra is taking full responsibility and is handling the clean-up. The gas well was presently shut in with a new piece of tubing in place. The operator reported less than one barrel of oil that was released from this well. It was difficult to say how much oil was released from a spill like this where the production fluids are spread over the land area by the venting (blowing) gas. There was a 60 yard x 35 yard area around the well where the oil mist had been scraped off the ground surface. No residual of any kind was seen. There was however an oil residual on the leaves of the trees for an approximate 80 yard stretch. I contacted Jason Nowakowski from Centerra regarding the clean-up and the ownership of the trees on the field edge. He said they have hauled the soil back to their shop for proper disposal. He also said that he would have to get back to me on the ownership of the trees.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 12/23/2025
Comments: On 12/23/2025, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 33 degrees, overcast and lightly snowing when I arrived on location. Snowfall had impacted the region in the last 24 hours, depositing approximately 3 inches on the location. The original south pad for the Taft 851 1V well has been returned to original grade. The plugged well monument witnessed during previous inspections was not visible. Stormwater diversion berms have been installed north and west of the original pad. Due to snow cover, stabilization could not be assessed for the constructed areas. Patterson drilling rig #805 has been towered down and removed from the north pad, having drilled eight new gas wells to total depth. Most of the drilling equipment has been removed from the site. Crews were on site, cleaning up the surface of the drilling mats and pumping out the well cellars. 40 frac tanks, seven rolloff dumpsters, two vac boxes, and four cement silos remain on site. Five wells have been completed at the site and were staged for production. Sand separators and two frac tanks remain attached to these wells. I did witness a 4' x 16' x 2" deep puddle of liquid on the unprotected pad surface north of the five GPUs that field tested at 1953 uS conductance. I reported this to a maintenance worker who relayed it to the Seneca site manager, Cory Miller.Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Sediment trap 3 and the sediment basin did have standing water/ice. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations.The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth. I left the site at 1600 hours.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/22/2026 to OIL & GAS MGMT INC in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland county. 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.

Violation ID: 8271887
Permit API: 129-24171
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Allegheny Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/22/2026
Comments: On April 22, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up inspection of Oil and Gas Mgmt's Armstrong 2 gas well site located in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County.This inspection is following IR 4160648, which documents violations that were issued for heavily rusted production equipment due to their corrosion posing the risk of a spill and/or release.This inspection is also following IR 4183514, which documents the Department attempted to contact the Operator to discuss various violations on site/on the access road, however, the phone number on the well tag was not in service, therefore violations were issued at that time for inaccurate information on the well tag. A Notice of Violation Operator response has yet to be received for the violations issued during IR 4160648, and site conditions appear to be unchanged.The Department's assessment of the shared portion of this access road as well as the direct portion of this access road can be found in IR 4186406 and IR 4186412.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the Armstrong 2 well site to be overgrown with vegetation, the Department recommends the Operator maintain the vegetation within the well site to ensure the well site remains accessible. A well tag was observed to be fixed to a heavily rusted gas well that did not appear to have updated Operator information posted on it. Violations issued for an inaccurate well tag are being continued at this time.At the time of this inspection, a heavily rusted production tank was also observed on site and connected for production, no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this tank or gas wellhead at this time. The Department recommends the Operator monitor and maintain the structural integrity of the production tank and gas wellhead to ensure that corrosion does not worsen resulting in a release. Although no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed, a strong gas odor and hissing was still observed to be coming from the lower portion of the gas wellhead. Based on today's inspection, violations issues for heavily rusted production equipment posing the risk for a spill/release and for inaccurate operator information on the well tag/posting is to remain outstanding at this time.
